title: Walking Lunge
summary: Alternating forward lunges as you walk, for the quads and glutes.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.9 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.8 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.5 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.5 for abductors (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly abductors total.
Library rating 0.3 for hamstrings (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.

setup.text: Hold dumbbells at your sides and step forward into a long stride.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your front foot and step straight into the next lunge.

form_cues.cue: Lower the back knee toward the floor
Push through the front foot into the next step
Take controlled steps. Don't let your front knee cave inward.

mistakes.text: Taking short steps that push the front knee way past the toes with heels lifting.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Similar muscles; dumbbell instead of dumbbell.
Swap sheet: More stable, Less systemic fatigue, Easier to learn.
Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, More stable, Less systemic fatigue.
